subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test (Finwise)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@finwise.com>, Jake Morales <jake@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test (Finwise)

Hi Tara / Jake —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the deep dive on Finwise's latency and throughput goals. Per our call, here's a quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Recap (what you told us)
- Primary SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for standard generate endpoint; streaming responses (chunked SSE) for long-running responses with p95 of first-byte < 350ms.
- Throughput target: sustained 2000 req/s during peak window; concurrency target ~500 concurrent active requests.
- Acceptable error rate: <0.5% 5xx across test windows.
- Test routing: use the dedicated performance endpoint we provide; stick to model: redwood/llama-3-40b-quant (or compatible variant) for parity with production.

What Redwood will provide
- k6 and Locust example scripts (we'll attach) and a test account + API key scoped for the test.
- IP ranges to allowlist for the test (we'll provide CIDRs).
- A recommended 3-hour test window with a ramp (30m ramp-up, 2h steady, 30m cool-down) — we can adjust to your ops calendar.

Next steps / owners
1) Logan — share k6/Locust scripts + test account instructions (today) [ACTION: Logan]
2) Tara — confirm preferred test window (timezone & date) and any internal change freeze windows (by EOD Tue) [ACTION: Finwise]
3) Marissa / Rishi — provide the IP allowlist and test endpoint details; review scripts for any payload adjustments (by Wed) [ACTION: Redwood SRE/Perf]

Attachments: finwise_k6_script.js (k6), locustfile_finwise.py (locust), test_account_instructions.txt

If that all looks right I can provision the test credentials so you can kick off the first run.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0128

Thanks, Logan — this is perfect and matches what we discussed. A few clarifying points from our side:

- Test window: target next Friday 2027-04-30 01:00–04:00 PST (overnight for our transactional systems) — let us know if that conflicts with Redwood maintenance windows.
- We need whitelisted egress CIDRs for our infra team to allow responses back to our collector; can you provide both Redwood outbound ranges and the specific test IPs you'll use?
- For streaming: we will validate that chunked responses preserve event ordering; do you have a sample client we should use to validate SSE behavior?

Also, please send the test account + API key and the scripts so our SREs can run a dry run on Monday.

Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Platform Engineering | Finwise
tara@finwise.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test (Finwise)

Tara — thanks. Quick answers and attached items below.

1) Test window: Friday 2027-04-30 01:00–04:00 PST is good on our side; no scheduled maintenance on Redwood Dedicated for that window.

2) IP allowlist / outbound ranges:
- Test runner IPs (Finwise-accepted): 34.82.12.128/32, 34.82.12.129/32 (we will use these as the source IPs for the k6 cloud runs).
- Redwood egress ranges to Finwise collector (please allow): 35.199.0.0/16, 34.64.0.0/11.
- If you need a static NAT for callbacks we can enable a single NAT egress (request needed) — let me know.

3) Streaming client: we included a minimal Node SSE client in test_account_instructions.txt (section: streaming_client_example). That will validate chunk ordering and first-byte latency.

4) Test credentials: created a scoped API key: FINWISE-TEST-20270422 (note: we will send this via the Finwise secrets channel / DocuSign secure notes — do not post keys on email).

5) Scripts: attached finwise_k6_script.js and locustfile_finwise.py. The k6 script has a 30m ramp up, targets 2000 RPS across 10k virtual users in steady state; it includes a streaming scenario that hits /v1/stream and measures first-byte latency. The Locust file is for on-prem runs if you prefer running from your cluster.

Action items assigned:
- Marissa: please confirm the load-test endpoint hostname and port to supply to Finwise (ACTION: Marissa)
- Rishi: can you review the k6 ramp & thresholds and call out any suggested adjustments by Wed EOD? (ACTION: Rishi)

Attachments referenced: finwise_k6_script.js, locustfile_finwise.py, test_account_instructions.txt

Thanks —

--
